html:
Ilia Chavchavadze was a writer, publisher and public leader, born in 1837 in Kvareli in Kakheti, who led the Georgian national revival under Russian rule.

He studied in Saint Petersburg and came home with a new generation called the men of the sixties. He founded newspapers, a bank for nobles' land that funded schools and theatres, and the Society for the Spreading of Literacy among Georgians. His motto was fatherland, language and faith. He wrote poems, stories and essays, and helped make modern Georgian the language of print. He opposed both Russification and the Marxists rising in Georgia. He was murdered on the road near Tsitsamuri in 1907. The Georgian church made him a saint in 1987, honouring him as father of the nation, next to Tamar and David.
sum: Ilia Chavchavadze was a writer, publisher and public leader, born in 1837 in Kvareli in Kakheti, who led the Georgian national revival under Russian rule.
